statement: A Greek property transfer needs an engineer's confirmation about unauthorised constructions or uses (originally under Article 83 of Law 4495/2017, now tied to the Electronic Building Identity); constructions after 27 July 2011 generally cannot be legalised.
details: Sources disagree on the exact current certificate. Treat this as a flag for the notary and engineer, never as a conclusion.

statement: Since 1 January 2021, most buildings and independent units need an Electronic Building Identity (Law 4495/2017), completed by an authorised engineer, before their first transfer.
details: The engineer compiles the permit and revisions, approved plans, the energy certificate and the status of any arbitrary works. Add it to every sales dossier.

statement: Building permits in Greece are issued through the Technical Chamber's electronic system e-Άδειες under Law 4495/2017 (Articles 29, 33 and 36, as amended by Law 4759/2020); the category of the works decides the procedure.
details: Categories 1 and 2 can be issued automatically once the engineer files a complete electronic file and the building service gives prior approval.

statement: Presidential Decree 71/2019 replaced the former public-works contractor register (ΜΕΕΠ) with new registers, including the Technical Works Register of Enterprises (ΜΗ.Ε.Τ.Ε.), used to check bidders' capacity under Law 4412/2016.
details: Law-firm newsletter from 2019; check whether the registers are fully operational and amended.

statement: An energy performance certificate (ΠΕΑ, Law 4122/2013) is required to sell buildings or units over 50 m², with listed exemptions; the owner is responsible for it.
details: Sources differ on rentals. Secondary source; confirm with the energy inspector or the Ministry of Environment and Energy.

statement: Greek public and private works commonly secure performance and advance payments with bank letters of guarantee (εγγυητικές επιστολές) set by the contract documents.
details:
Record each guarantee's amount, beneficiary and expiry as a covenant and set a reminder before it lapses.

Source note: the cited page describes Law 4412/2016 generally; guarantee practice is general knowledge to verify with a Greek lawyer.

statement: Appeals against a preliminary approval of a building permit must be filed within 30 days of notification, before the Regional Councils for Urban Planning Issues and Disputes (Article 23 of Law 4495/2017).
details: Put the appeal deadline on the project calendar when a preliminary approval is received.

statement: Public works, supply and service contracts in Greece are governed by Law 4412/2016, which transposes the EU procurement directives.
details: Payment certifications (πιστοποιήσεις) and supplementary contracts in public works follow this law and the contract documents.

statement: Property transfers in Greece that are not subject to VAT pay transfer tax of about 3.09% (3% plus a municipal surcharge), generally on the higher of the price and the objective value.
details: Secondary source (real-estate firm). Confirm the base and the rate with the notary.

statement: Greece's standard VAT rate is 24%, but VAT on sales of new buildings is suspended until 31 December 2026 (Law 5246/2025); suspended sales pay transfer tax of about 3.09% instead, and the regime is optional for the developer.
details: Check per project whether the developer opted in, and watch for a decision on extension beyond 2026. Source is a VAT news service; confirm against the Government Gazette.
